//EventEnvelopeSigning: The host deliberately ships no signing key — EnvelopeIntegrityBroker refuses to construct without one (#392), which is what we want on an unconfigured host. The suite boots that same host, so it must supply a key of its own; this is it.
//ConnectionStrings: Test-only key, deliberately NOT one of the three production keys the portal reads
AcceptanceDatabaseBroker drops the catalogues it resolves, and any host or CI job that
configures the portal through the environment sets exactly those production names — so a
fixture that read them could be pointed at a real database and would drop it.
The Database given below is a TEMPLATE only. The broker replaces it with
Glory2Him.Security_Acceptance_<process id> so concurrent runs cannot collide, and hands
those to the host under the production keys from
an in-memory configuration layer. Schemas are created by the host itself: Core and Identity
migrate on start, EventHighway builds its own store on first use.
One template for all three: the portal boots them from one server, so a key per store would
add nothing but three places to diverge. Point the suite elsewhere by editing this one value.
